title: Ask for review of a real estate assessment and appeal to the Board of Equalization
question: I think my property assessment is too high. How do I get it reviewed or appealed?
office: Department of Finance & Budget, Real Estate Office (County Assessor)
summary: Albemarle County reassesses all real estate every year at fair market value as of January 1, and the County Assessor (Department of Finance & Budget) mails notices by the end of January. Start by calling the Assessor's Office to talk with your appraiser. For a formal review, file the written review request form by the date on the notice (for 2026, March 2 by 5 p.m., or carry a postmark of that date); the appraiser inspects inside and out and answers by letter. You can also appeal to the Board of Equalization, using a form available only from the Assessor's Office, by the Board deadline on the notice (for 2026, March 30, or 30 days after the Assessor's letter, whichever is later). After the Board, you can apply to the Albemarle Circuit Court, and the court's final judgment can be appealed to the Court of Appeals of Virginia. Keep paying the tax on the regular due dates while a review or appeal is pending.

steps.step: The County Assessor mails the annual reassessment notice
steps.who: Department of Finance & Budget, Office of the County Assessor
steps.how: Every parcel is reassessed each year at 100% of fair market value as of January 1. The notice shows the new and prior values and, as state law requires, when and where to present objections and the appeal deadlines. The 2026 notices were mailed on Friday, January 23, 2026; owners enrolled in e-statements receive them by email. Values can also be looked up in the county's GIS viewer.
steps.deadline: By the end of January each year (2026 notices mailed January 23, 2026); state law requires mailing at least 15 days before the hearing on objections (Va. Code § 58.1-3330(A))

steps.step: Optional first step: call the appraiser assigned to the property
steps.who: Property owner or authorized agent; Office of the County Assessor
steps.how: Call the County Assessor's Office (Monday to Friday, 8 a.m. to 5 p.m.; 711 for the hearing or speech impaired), or email the office mailbox with your name, phone number and parcel ID. The appraiser confirms the property data, explains the valuation and sets up an inspection if the description looks wrong. The office aims to return calls and emails within 48 hours. Call before visiting the office.
steps.quote: Please call the Assessor’s Office at 434-296-5856 to speak to the appraiser assigned to your property.

steps.step: Optional: see the assessment records for the property
steps.who: Property owner or authorized agent; Office of the County Assessor
steps.how: Ask to see the property appraisal card and working papers, the methodology and comparable sales used, and a written explanation of any increase. An agent must submit the original current-year Letter of Authorization with any request for copies of assessment worksheets or other information about the assessment.
steps.deadline: Appraisal cards are open for inspection after the reassessment notice is mailed (Va. Code § 58.1-3331(A))
steps.quote: the assessing officer shall provide a written explanation or justification for an increase in the property's assessed value.

steps.step: Prepare the written request for the County Assessor's review
steps.who: Property owner or tenant, or an agent with a notarized Letter of Authorization
steps.how: Use the county's Real Estate Assessment Review Form, one form per parcel. The 2025 form (the latest copy found) asks you to tick the reasons and back them up: fair market value (comparable sales), uniformity (comparable assessments), errors in the property description, or income and expense statements for income-producing property. It also requires your opinion of value as of January 1, a phone number and an email address. On the 2025 form the applicant may be the owner, an agent or a tenant; an applicant who is not the owner or tenant must attach an original Letter of Authorization, with the notarized signature of the owner or tenant, for the current year. The 2026 Letter of Authorization must be signed by the owner of record or, for a corporation, an officer authorized to act for it; management companies and other third parties may not sign it.

steps.step: File the review request with the County Assessor by the deadline on the notice
steps.how: Deliver or mail the form to the Office of the County Assessor, 401 McIntire Road, Room 243, Charlottesville, VA 22902. The 2025 form also lists the office's email address and fax number. A separate form is needed for each parcel.
steps.deadline: March 2, 2026: received by close of business (5 p.m.) or postmarked by that date (the 2026 date; 2025's was February 28, and each year's date is printed on the notice. February 28, 2026 was a Saturday; Va. Code § 1-210(E) carries a deadline that falls on a weekend to the next business day)

steps.step: The appraiser inspects the property and the Assessor answers in writing
steps.who: Office of the County Assessor (the appraiser assigned to the property)
steps.how: The office considers what you sent and must inspect the property inside and out; an appraiser contacts you to set the appointment (weekdays 8:30 a.m. to 4 p.m. on the 2025 form). The 2025 form says the review is canceled if you do not respond within 15 business days of being contacted. The decision comes by letter. If you accept it, nothing more is needed.
steps.deadline: No time limit for the decision is stated; on the 2025 form the review is canceled if the owner does not respond within 15 business days of the office's contact

steps.step: Appeal to the Board of Equalization
steps.who: Property owner or authorized agent; Board of Equalization (six members, each appointed by one member of the Board of Supervisors)
steps.how: Ask the County Assessor's Office for the Board of Equalization appeal form; it is not posted online. You may file it while an Assessor's review is still pending. Under state law, a hearing on a residential property cannot be denied for lack of information on the application if the application gives the address, the parcel number and your proposed assessed value; for commercial, multifamily or industrial property appealed on fair market value, the same protection also requires documentation of any applicable assessment methodologies with the application. The Board may consider income and expense statements and market sales through December 31 that reach it by the filing deadline, but no studies or analyses published after December 31. The Board cannot decide land use (use-value) qualification.
steps.deadline: March 30, 2026, or within 30 days from the date of the County Assessor's letter answering a review request, whichever is later; received by 5 p.m. or postmarked by the deadline, but the county says a mailed form must actually arrive to be valid

steps.step: Get the Assessor's records before the Board hearing (homes with fewer than four units)
steps.who: Property owner; Office of the County Assessor
steps.how: For a residential property with fewer than four units, the Assessor must send a notice at least 45 days before the hearing explaining your right to the assessment records and to ask for a physical inspection. Ask for the records in writing. If they are not provided in time, the Assessor must put its records and appraisal testimony in evidence before you present your case. For commercial, multifamily or industrial property, any request by the Assessor to raise the value must be noticed at least 14 days before the hearing. If you contest such a requested increase, the Assessor must either withdraw it or give the Board an appraisal by an independent licensed general real estate appraiser, unless the increase rests on mistakes of fact or on information you were asked for but did not provide.
steps.deadline: Assessor must provide the records within 15 days of a written request
steps.quote: The assessing officer shall provide such records within 15 days of a written request by the taxpayer or his duly authorized representative.

steps.step: Present your case at the Board of Equalization hearing
steps.who: Board of Equalization; property owner or agent; County Assessor
steps.how: Board sittings are public and announced at least seven days ahead in a newspaper and by posting at the courthouse and libraries or voting precincts. The County Assessor testifies about how the value was set. The Board presumes the Assessor's value is correct; you must show by a preponderance of the evidence that it is above fair market value, or not uniform, and was not reached by accepted appraisal practice. In commercial, industrial or multifamily cases a member with real estate, building, legal or financial expertise must sit unless you waive it. The Board can raise a value as well as lower it. The county posted 2026 Board recordings dated April 22 to July 13.
steps.deadline: Public notice of each sitting at least seven days before it (Va. Code § 58.1-3378)

steps.how: The Board increases, decreases or affirms the assessment by order, and sends copies of orders that change an assessment to the owner and the assessing officer. It cannot raise a value without first notifying the owner and giving a chance to object, and on commercial, multifamily or industrial property it cannot raise one unless the Assessor recommends the increase under Va. Code § 58.1-3379. If the value is lowered after the tax was paid, the owner is entitled to a refund of the excess.
steps.deadline: All reassessment appeals must be disposed of by September 1 of the assessment year (Albemarle County Code § 15-702(D), as stated by the county)

steps.step: If you still disagree, apply to the Albemarle Circuit Court
steps.who: Property owner (taxpayer); Albemarle Circuit Court Clerk's Office
steps.how: File an application to correct an erroneous assessment in the Clerk's Office at the Albemarle County Courthouse, 350 Park Street, with the Cover Sheet for Filing Civil Actions (tick Taxes, Correct Erroneous State/Local); the Clerk requires a cover sheet with civil filings. Name 'Albemarle County' as the locality; the County Attorney defends. The court presumes the Assessor's or the Board's value is correct, and court fees apply.
steps.deadline: Within three years from the last day of the tax year, or within one year from the date of the assessment, whichever is later (Va. Code §§ 58.1-3984(A), 58.1-3382)
steps.fee: Court filing fees (amount not stated by the county; see fees)
steps.quote: (a) within three years from the last day of the tax year for which any such assessment is made, (b) within one year from the date of the assessment

steps.how: A judge hears the case without a jury. If the court finds the assessment erroneous, and the error was not caused by the owner's wilful failure or refusal to give the assessing office the information the law requires, it may order the assessment corrected. The court may lower the value to fair market value, and must raise it if it finds the value below fair market value. If the tax was already paid, the court must order a refund with interest. The clerk certifies the change so the land book is corrected.
steps.quote: the court may reduce the assessment to what in its opinion based on the evidence is the fair market value of the property involved.

steps.step: Keep paying the real estate tax on the regular due dates
steps.who: Property owner; Department of Finance & Budget, Office of Revenue Administration
steps.how: The county's pages do not say that a review or appeal postpones the due dates. A late payment brings a penalty of 10 percent (at least $10), plus 10% yearly interest, and the county's penalty policy lists an incorrect bill among the reasons for which penalty and interest cannot be waived. If the value is later lowered, state law gives an exoneration or a refund (Va. Code §§ 58.1-3385, 58.1-3987).
steps.deadline: June 25 and December 5 each year (moved to the next business day if the date falls on a weekend; December 5, 2026 is a Saturday, so the second 2026 installment is due Monday, December 7, 2026)

caveats: Albemarle County's website (www.albemarle.org) refuses automated readers, so the county pages and PDFs cited here are Internet Archive copies: they show the pages as they were when copied. The live pages may have changed since; confirm on them before you act. The County's Terms and Conditions bar reposting its content without written permission, so the County's own words are not reprinted on this page; each step links the County page instead.

Deadlines are for 2026: the Assessor's review by March 2, 2026, and the Board of Equalization by March 30, 2026 (or 30 days after the Assessor's letter). In 2025 they were February 28 and March 31, 2025. The page copy of 2026-01-18 still showed the 2025 dates. State law requires each year's deadlines to be printed on the notice (Va. Code § 58.1-3378); the 2026 notice itself was not seen.

Review form: the county says the review request form is on www.albemarle.org/assessor (which redirects to the Real Estate Tax Assessments page) or in the office. The 2025 'Request for Assessment Review Fillable Form' was linked in February 2025, but no 2026 version was linked on any archived copy read and none was found in the archive index. Step s4 describes the 2025 form; get the current one from the office.

Board of Equalization form: the county says appeal forms are available only by contacting the County Assessor's Office, so no form URL exists. Whether the office accepts electronic filing (Va. Code § 58.1-3378 allows it) is not stated.

Postmark rule: the county says the appeal form must be received by 5 p.m. or postmarked by the deadline, and also that a mailed form must actually arrive to be valid, regardless of the postmark. Va. Code § 58.1-3378 says the postmark date of a mailed paper form counts as the date of receipt. Read together, a form postmarked by the deadline that arrives afterwards appears timely under both, while a form that never arrives was never filed; this reading was not confirmed with the office. Delivering early, or keeping proof of mailing, avoids the question.

The 30-day floor: Va. Code § 58.1-3378 says the Board filing date may not be earlier than 30 days after 'the termination of the date set by the assessing officer to hear objections'. The 2026 Board date (March 30) is 28 days after the 2026 review deadline (March 2). The county page copies of 2025-02-26 and 2026-01-18 gave the review deadline as 'February 28 of the year in which the assessment takes effect'; February 28, 2026 was a Saturday, so March 2 looks like that date carried to the next business day under Va. Code § 1-210(E), and March 30 is 30 days after February 28. Whether the review deadline is the objection date the statute means, and how a carried-over date bears on the floor, was not determined. The later-of rule separately gives anyone who asked for a review 30 days from the Assessor's letter.

Local ordinance not checked: Albemarle's Code of Ordinances is published only on Municode, whose CivicPlus terms forbid automated access and republication, so no County Code text is quoted. Sections 15-700, 15-702, 15-702(D) and 15-103 are given as the county describes them: on its Real Estate Tax Assessments and Important Dates pages, and in the Board of Supervisors staff report of January 21, 2026 (Legistar matter 8447). The quoted staff-report sentences come from Legistar's plain text, where section signs appear as replacement characters; quotes were cut to avoid them. The 2019 recodification staff report (Legistar file 19-237, matter 3565) says new § 15-702 would extend the Board deadline to March 30, but its proposed ordinance has not been checked. Whether § 15-702 was adopted as proposed, and its current wording, are not confirmed.

Board of Equalization type: the FAQ flyer says the Board has six members, each appointed by one member of the Board of Supervisors, one per magisterial district. That fits Va. Code § 58.1-3371 (county executive form: the board of supervisors appoints, up to the number of districts, terms ending December 31), not a permanent board appointed by the circuit court under § 58.1-3373. This is an inference from the flyer; the County Code was not read.

Fees: no fee for the Assessor's review or the Board appeal was found, and the county pages say neither that there is one nor that there is none. For court, the county states no amount. Which Va. Code § 17.1-275 category the Clerk uses for a § 58.1-3984 application is not confirmed: (A)(26), $60 for civil actions without a money-damages claim, or (A)(13), $100 to $300 by amount sought. Other costs may apply, such as service of process. A notary fee for the Letter of Authorization is not covered here.

Decision times: no time limit is stated for the Assessor's review decision. The county says the Board must dispose of all appeals by September 1; no rule was found for how soon the Board mails its order, beyond the 'transmit promptly' duty in Va. Code § 58.1-3384.

Direct court route: Va. Code §§ 58.1-3350 and 58.1-3984(A) allow going straight to circuit court where the Board is not a prerequisite. Whether Albemarle's code makes the Board a prerequisite was not determined. The county's Notice of Taxpayer Appeal Rights page says 'the taxpayer may go to the local circuit court at any stage of the administrative review', but that page is about corrections of Finance Department assessments of other taxes (personal property, business license and similar), not real estate reassessment appeals.

Correction route (escalation rung 6): Va. Code § 58.1-3980(A) reaches real estate only where the error was made by the assessing official or is a factual error in a general reassessment. Whether the county handles such requests through the County Assessor or the Finance Department's correction process, and whether it treats an annual assessment as a 'general reassessment' for this purpose, was not confirmed.

Paying during an appeal: the county pages do not say whether a review or appeal postpones the June 25 and December 5 due dates. Va. Code § 58.1-3958 pauses collection only during an administrative appeal under § 58.1-3980 filed within 90 days of the assessment. Whether an Assessor's review counts was not confirmed.

Risk of an increase: the Board can increase as well as decrease an assessment (Va. Code §§ 58.1-3379(A), 58.1-3381(A); the county's flyer says the same), and the court must raise one it finds below fair market value (§ 58.1-3987).

Income-producing property: the county sends Commercial Income and Expense Survey forms by July 1, due back October 1. Va. Code § 58.1-3294 bars using required but unfiled income and expense data in court, though it may still go to the Board by its filing deadline. The 2025 review form asked for three prior years of statements.
Land use: the county says the Board of Equalization cannot decide land use (use-value) qualification; that is a separate process.

Letter of Authorization: two 2026 copies are linked, one on the Real Estate Tax Assessments page (document 28857, read) and one on the Documents page (document 28869, not read). The form requires notarization; Va. Code § 58.1-3380 presumes a notarized owner's letter is a valid designation.
Board recordings: the county page lists 2026 Board of Equalization recordings from April 22 to July 13. One recording link points to a staff member's personal file share and is not recorded here.

Va. Code § 58.1-3250 (a legal hint for this task) sets the reassessment cycle for cities only and does not apply to Albemarle County. The county rules are §§ 58.1-3252 and 58.1-3253, under which the county assesses annually by ordinance.

Court of Appeals: only the statutory route and the 30-day notice of appeal (Va. Code § 8.01-675.3) are recorded. The Rules of the Supreme Court of Virginia (Part 5A) and appeal fees are not covered here.

Privacy: the county pages, the 2026 staff report and the court page name staff, the Clerk and the judges; none are recorded. Only the office's published mailbox (CountyAssessor@), the payments mailbox, office phone and fax lines, office addresses and portals are kept.

State-law quotes are matched to Open US Law's copy of the Code of Virginia (none of these sections carries an effective-until date). They keep that copy's spacing before punctuation after cross-references (for example '§ 58.1-3330 .'). The text has not been compared with law.lis.virginia.gov.

County site terms: the County's Terms and Conditions page (Internet Archive copy of 2026-07-20) authorizes anyone 'to read the County website for information' but bars reposting or reusing site content without written permission. County quotes are kept to one sentence each, for citation; whether publishing them needs the County's permission is a decision for the project owner.

Timing: as of this check (2026-10-11), the 2026 review and Board of Equalization deadlines have passed. For a 2026 assessment, the remaining routes are the correction application for the assessing office's own errors (escalation rung 6) and the Circuit Court (step s11), within the time limits stated there. For 2027, use the dates printed on the 2027 notice, expected by the end of January 2027.

corrections: Quotes: all 84 original quotes were checked. The 67 state-law quotes are substrings of I.text_of for the cited section (whitespace normalised), and their subsection labels match the text. The 17 County and staff-report quotes were matched against the Internet Archive copies of the cited albemarle.org pages and PDFs (www.albemarle.org still answers HTTP 403) and against the Legistar Web API text of matter 8447, re-fetched on 2026-10-11. Two flyer quotes (s2, s5) had straight apostrophes where the flyer has curly ones (Assessor’s); they now match the flyer exactly. Five state-law quotes were added and checked the same way: § 58.1-3379(C) (no studies published after December 31), § 58.1-3379(D) (withdraw the increase request or provide an independent appraisal), § 58.1-3381(A) (no increase on commercial, multifamily or industrial property unless the assessor recommends it), § 58.1-3987 (no correction where the owner wilfully withheld required information) and § 1-210(E) (a deadline on a weekend moves to the next business day).

s7: the draft said a residential application 'cannot be refused' for lack of information. Va. Code § 58.1-3378 protects the hearing: it 'shall not be denied on the basis of a lack of information'. For commercial, multifamily and industrial property, documentation of the assessment methodologies is a condition of that protection, not a general filing requirement. The draft said income and expense statements and December sales 'count only if' the Board has them by the deadline; § 58.1-3379(C) is permissive, so the step now says the Board may consider them if they arrive by the deadline. The bar on studies published after December 31 is added.

s12: the draft said the court 'can order a refund with interest'. Va. Code § 58.1-3987 says that if the tax has been paid the court 'shall order that it be refunded', so the step now says must. It also adds the statute's condition that the error was not caused by the owner's wilful failure or refusal to furnish required information.

s10: adds the § 58.1-3381(A) limit on raising commercial, multifamily or industrial assessments. s8: adds the § 58.1-3379(D) rule that a contested increase request must be withdrawn or backed by an independent licensed appraisal, with its two exceptions.

s4: the 2025 review form lets a tenant apply as well as the owner or an agent, and asks for a Letter of Authorization notarized by the owner or tenant. The 2026 Letter of Authorization must be signed by the owner of record or an authorized corporate officer; management companies and other third parties may not sign. s3: the Letter of Authorization goes with any request for worksheets or assessment information (the form says 'with', not 'before').

s5: notes that February 28, 2026 was a Saturday and that Va. Code § 1-210(E) carries a weekend deadline to the next business day. The 2025-02-26 and 2026-01-18 page copies stated the review deadline as 'February 28 of the year in which the assessment takes effect'. s13: December 5, 2026 is a Saturday, so under the county's weekend rule the second 2026 installment is due Monday, December 7, 2026. The step also adds that the county's penalty policy lists an incorrect bill among the reasons penalty and interest cannot be waived.

Summary: the draft called the Circuit Court 'the last step', but escalation rung 7 goes on to the Court of Appeals. The summary now says so, marks the dates as the 2026 notice dates, and says to keep paying the tax during an appeal. Escalation rung 6: adds the § 58.1-3984(A) court window of one year from the official's final determination.

Caveats: the 30-day-floor caveat put 'date set to hear objections' in quotation marks, which is not the statute's wording; it now quotes 'the termination of the date set by the assessing officer to hear objections' and adds the February 28 base date. The postmark caveat now gives a reading under which the county's statements and § 58.1-3378 fit together, marked as unconfirmed. New caveats cover the County's Terms and Conditions and timing as of this check. Sources add the Terms and Conditions copy and Va. Code § 1-210.
